external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker, including colleagues using their own devices at home.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify whether colleagues are employees, contractors, or another category.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

external_entities.name: franchise stores
external_entities.description: Stores whose colleagues are allowed to sign in through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: System that supplies colleague group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: own identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider belonging to franchise colleagues that vouches for their sign-in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not identify which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, maintains colleague group membership, accepts franchise identity-provider sign-ins, and writes sign-in events to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: Nobody has written down whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: Application that uses the token's groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: Store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: Log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. Nobody has written down whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Colleagues submit a sign-in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token containing the colleague's staff id and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: Tokens are good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: Colleagues provide their token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public half
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the identity broker's public signing-key half to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls overnight group-membership and leaver changes from the HR system.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague's sign-in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker accesses the signing key kept in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains its directory of colleagues and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the audit log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Network zone where the identity broker and store admin console run, and where the broker's key store, directory, and audit log are placed by the description.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: colleagues' own devices at home
trust_boundaries.description: External device and home location from which colleagues may sign in to the identity broker.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: Zone controlled by the franchise stores and containing the franchise colleagues and their own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source says the key store holds a signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source says the directory holds colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it records sign-ins associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source says the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
